stories.completionNotes: DONE (passes:true). BL-023 was RESOLVED (commit 5500876: TSL2591 live+I2C-addressable @0x29, verified on the Pi 2026-07-22) -- built the REAL feed, not a fallback. (1) CONFIG: flipped pi.bus.enabled + pi.sensors.light.enabled ON (connect-when-wired); IMU left OFF (dead clone boards -> graceful-absent reader stays silent, light isolated per conditionalOutcome). validate_config OK. (2) BRIDGE: new src/pi/sensors/light_state_bridge.py LightStateBridge -- a PURE bus consumer (Atlas DELTA-2: reader owns the state file, display never touches sensor). Subscribes raw.light.lux LOSSY (display needs only freshest), drains on its own daemon thread (mirrors EdrPersistenceSubscriber), writes states/light {lux, ts} atomically via the shared boot_state_emitter ensureStatesDir+writeStateAtomic (mirrors US-480-a states/ writers, no dup). eclipse-states-http serves it AS-IS with no server change (its do_GET already serves any file in statesDir, token-gated). SEAM SHAPE for Atlas confirm: file=/run/eclipse-obd/states/light, payload={lux: float|null, ts: ISO-8601} -- mirrors the existing writers. (3) HONEST-INSTRUMENT carried through the seam: saturation (lux=None from sensor_reader._readLux) -> JSON null (never inf/0.0); non-finite coerced to None (defense-in-depth _coerceLux); ts = SAMPLE read-time (not write-time) so a stalled feed goes honestly stale -> US-483-b consumer falls back rather than trusting a frozen lux. (4) RUN-MODEL: orchestrator-invoked in _startEdrSensorPath (subscribe+start BEFORE readers publish so no early sample missed; STREAM has no history), stopped in _shutdownDataLogger. Opens NO I2C device + NO OBD connection -> cannot re-introduce the A-17 second-connection race (VC3 satisfied by construction: no new obd.OBD()/connect caller). (5) Rule-10: architecture.md 10.8.2 documents the bridge + records the config flip. GREEN in-loop: 10 new bridge tests + 4 test_lifecycle_bus_wiring tests = 14 passed; ruff clean on all touched files; validate_config passed. GATES for PM/integration + Pi-runtime: mypy NOT run (not installed on this dev host -- PM/integration typecheck gate; module is fully type-hinted + ruff-clean). VC1 (ls+curl states/light live 200) + VC2 (cover/shine sensor -> lux tracks) are PI-RUNTIME gates (real Pi + engine/bench power + live TSL2591). Atlas SEAM CONFIRM is a heads-up (he APPROVED DELTA-2 pure-consumer) -- built per CIO directive on the approved pattern; flag the {lux,ts} shape for his confirm. Enables US-483-b (consumer) -- its dependency is now met.

filesActuallyTouched: config.json (NEW pi.display.autoDim.* grounded params; distinct from live pi.display.brightness hardware-backlight scalar)

stories.completionNotes: DONE (passes:true). Dependency US-483-a (states/light producer) was MET. Built the full pure-consumer chain per Atlas DELTA-2 (display reads only the reader-owned state file, never the sensor). (1) CONFIG-KEY COLLISION RESOLVED: the story named pi.display.brightness.* but that key is the LIVE 0-100 hardware-backlight scalar (adafruit adapter helpers.py:238 validates int 0-100, power_display.py dims it) -- converting it to a nested object would break those. Put the 0.0-1.0 software-dim curve under a NEW pi.display.autoDim.* object (all leaf names kept: luxMin/luxFull/minLevel/defaultLevel/alarmFloorLevel/luxStaleSec/curve). GROUNDED: luxMin=3.0 (civil-twilight dark ~3.4lux), luxFull=1000.0 (overcast daylight ~1000lux); levels are Iris-tunable. (2) SSOT + PARAMETERIZED (CIO 'config not code'): config.json = tuning SSOT; validator DEFAULTS mirror (b044-exempt) + _validateDisplayAutoDim rejects unsafe values (levels must be in [0,1]; luxFull>luxMin>0; curve in {logarithmic,linear}) -- a bad alarmFloor can't silently ship. (3) CONSUMER (carousel.js pure fns): brightnessLevel = clamp(minLevel, brightnessCurve(lux), 1.0) fresh, else defaultLevel (honest fallback: absent/stale/null->default, NEVER fabricated auto); ALARM FLOOR = brightnessAlarmActive(dtc) (real STOP hero present, reuses ribbonView honest classifier) raises level to >= alarmFloorLevel regardless of lux (floor RAISES only, never caps). freshLux honors ts vs luxStaleSec (US-483-a ts=sample-read-time -> stalled feed goes stale->default). Applied as CSS var --display-brightness -> filter:brightness() on #screen (black bars stay black; #stage transform is the nearer containing block so US-482 scaling untouched). (4) CONFIG->BROWSER SEAM ('config change, not code'): eclipse-states-http injects pi.display.autoDim into dashboard.html at serve time via the QUOTED "__DISPLAY_AUTODIM__" placeholder (mirrors the __SPLASH_TOKEN__ SSOT seam) -- states_http_server.loadDisplayAutoDimConfig reads config.json fail-safe (raw json.load, no secrets/validator dep; ANY error->None->carousel's built-in grounded defaults, which mirror config.json). main() gains --config (default 'config.json', resolves against the unit WorkingDirectory). No second OBD/I2C connection opened anywhere (A-17 safe by construction). (5) Rule-10: architecture.md 10.8.2 documents the consumer + injection seam. GREEN in-loop: 33 new tests (22 brightness + 9 config + 2 injection) + full touched-area suite (tests/ui + tests/pi/splash + test_config_validator = 287 passed/1 skipped); ruff clean on all touched python; validate_config OK; carousel.js loads under node (probe tests pass = syntax valid). GATES: mypy = PM/integration (not installed on dev host; states_http_server fully type-hinted+ruff-clean). VC1 (cover sensor->dims toward minLevel) + VC2 (STOP takeover + cover->held>=0.40) + VC3 (stale feed->holds default, no fake auto) are PI-RUNTIME gates (real Pi + live TSL2591 + engine/bench power). DEPLOY HEADS-UP for PM: the eclipse-states-http.service ExecStart doesn't pass --config, so it uses the default 'config.json' relative to WorkingDirectory=/home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01 -- config.json is at that repo root so tuning DOES propagate on service restart; if the deployed WorkingDirectory ever differs, pass --config explicitly (else it fail-safes to the JS grounded defaults = correct out-of-box, just not tunable). Committed 1720bc8.
acceptance: display reads states/light {lux, ts} (never the sensor directly); brightness = clamp(minLevel, curve(lux), 1.0)

GROUNDED + PARAMETERIZED values in config (NOT hardcoded) -- add these keys with grounded defaults (illuminance references cited in the story notes): pi.display.brightness.luxMin=3.0 (lux<=this -> min; grounded = civil-twilight dark limit ~3.4lux), luxFull=1000.0 (lux>=this -> full; grounded = overcast-day ~1000lux), minLevel=0.15 (calm-screen dim floor), defaultLevel=0.70 (fixed fallback), luxStaleSec=10 (lux older -> fallback), curve='logarithmic' (perceptual, between luxMin..luxFull). Iris owns curve tuning; these are tunable via config, no code change

ALARM FLOOR (load-bearing safety): pi.display.brightness.alarmFloorLevel=0.40 -- brightness NEVER drops below this while a real active STOP ribbon/takeover is present, regardless of lux (a UI guard independent of the lux value)
HONEST FALLBACK: states/light absent OR ts older than luxStaleSec -> hold defaultLevel + show NO fabricated 'auto' behavior (honest instrument)
Iris AC-7: brightness tracks live lux when fresh; absent/stale -> fixed default (no fake auto); dimming never takes a STOP below its legible floor
consumes the state file only; pi/UI tests green (incl. a test that a STOP + dark-lux holds >= alarmFloorLevel)
